The Wikipedia page has a reference to the R documentation for clogit:

https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/survival/html/clogit.html

The details there discusses how the model can be reformulated as a Cox model and estimated as a coxph model; the work seems to lie in restructuring the data and adding some dummy variables.

Finn

messages.author: 2f6c5eed34f4bc17
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] conditional logistic regression
parts:
Does INLA do proportional hazards models? The likelihood for each data point depends on more than one node in the latent field. My understanding was that INLA fits survival models by directly estimating the hazard function, and hence these types of models which have likelihoods which are of the same functional form as a Cox PH partial likelihood can't be fit using the INLA software using the same tricks used by survival::clogit, mgcv::gam, and so on.

Alex
